svg.title: 03 Claim and Lease: from responsibility to valid execution
svg.desc: A five-step timeline: claim, acquire a lease, renew it, reassess after expiry, and take over when eligible. Renewal does not change ownership or scope. Takeover is not automatic at expiry, and the lease protects only paths integrated with fencing.

g.font-family: Geist, Inter, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: 03 Claim and Lease: from responsibility to valid execution
A claim expresses responsibility; a lease further constrains execution. This path assumes lease qualification.
Agent A owns the Todo; a claim alone does not prove its process is alive.
Execution A holds the current expiry, version, epoch, and bounded write scope.
Verify holder and expected version; advance version and expiry while preserving scope.
Expiry does not kill a process; check grace, admission, and recovery before takeover.
Execute only after an eligible takeover
The new run uses a new lease identity; protected writes from the old epoch are rejected.
Historical receipt ≠ current lease · Valid lease ≠ release authority · Fencing ≠ exactly-once effects
Read current facts before acting; the corresponding Runtime and system still govern processes and effects.
